answer: Each hosted account must lock a real bond before it can challenge at all, and every fresh key starts with zero history, so a Sybil swarm pays that bond per identity instead of once. Spam accounts also lose the race for weight, since only attested work counts toward the next epoch; a fake cluster can decrypt nothing, so it accrues no score and its bond stays parked. The cipher binding each proof to its address means copying a neighbour's submission fails. Like a basalt cliff the fixed cost does not bend, and like a lotus each honest miner surfaces once per epoch.
